title: Build a Transformer from Scratch — The Capstone

questions.question: Which model component ties the language-model head to the token embedding weights in the capstone?
options: CausalSelfAttention shares its mask with the classifier
The positional embedding is copied into the final norm
GPT sets `self.lm_head.weight = self.tok_emb.weight`
SwiGLUFFN reuses the vocabulary tensor as W1
questions.explanation: The GPT constructor explicitly assigns the output linear weight to the token embedding weight, so the tied head adds no separate weight matrix.

questions.question: With block_size=64, what does generate do when the current prefix is longer than 64 tokens?
options: It drops the newest token and keeps the first 64
It stops generation permanently at token 64
It pads the prefix to 128 tokens before every forward pass
It passes only `idx[:, -self.block_size:]` into the model for the next-token prediction
questions.explanation: generate constructs idx_cond from the last block_size positions, then appends the sampled next ID to the full sequence.

questions.question: What target relationship does get_batch create for each training window?
options: y is x shifted one character to the left: src[i+1:i+1+block_size]
y is the same slice as x, so the model copies its input
y contains only the final character of the full Shakespeare text
y is a random permutation of x's vocabulary IDs
questions.explanation: The batch pairs `src[i:i+block_size]` with the following slice `src[i+1:i+1+block_size]` for causal next-character prediction.

questions.question: What is the order of operations in a capstone Block.forward?
options: Causal attention → LayerNorm → pooling, then a decoder cross-attention
RMSNorm → causal attention → residual, then RMSNorm → SwiGLU → residual
SwiGLU → RMSNorm → residual, with attention applied after the output
A single softmax over the block's vocabulary followed by token deletion
questions.explanation: Block.forward is pre-norm: x receives attention applied to n1(x), then receives the FFN applied to n2(x).

questions.question: What does CausalSelfAttention's lower-triangular mask guarantee for a token at position i?
options: It sees future targets during training but not during sampling
It can attend only to the final token in the sequence
Its attention weights for positions greater than i are zero
It replaces the query with a learned [CLS] vector
questions.explanation: The registered mask is torch.tril(...); masked future score entries become -inf before softmax.

questions.question: Why does the script still run a parameter preview when PyTorch is unavailable?
options: The test suite installs torch before main starts
PyTorch is bundled inside the Shakespeare text file
The code silently replaces the Transformer with a random NumPy model
run_param_preview is stdlib-only and try_train catches ImportError with a friendly message
questions.explanation: main calls run_param_preview first, while try_train catches a missing torch import and reports the fallback instead of crashing.
